holidays.name: National Bobblehead Day
holidays.description: A nodding celebration of those wobbly-headed collectibles that bob along on dashboards and desks everywhere. Fans display their favorite figures and give a little nod of appreciation.
holidays.origin: Bobblehead Day is an unofficial observance, popularized by collectors and fans of the toys. Nodding-head figures date back to 18th-century Germany and Russia, and the modern bobblehead surged in popularity in the 1960s, particularly with sports figures.
holidays.funFact: The first Major League Baseball bobblehead giveaways took place in the 1960s, and the 'Nodders' of that era were made of papier-mâché and later ceramic before plastic took over.

holidays.name: National Tempura Day
holidays.description: A crispy, golden celebration of lightly battered and deep-fried shrimp and vegetables. Perfect for dunking in dipping sauce and crunching with abandon.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday observed by fans of Japanese cuisine. Tempura was introduced to Japan by Portuguese traders and missionaries in the 16th century, who fried foods during Lent, known as 'quatuor tempora'.
holidays.funFact: The word 'tempura' is believed to come from the Latin 'tempora,' meaning 'times,' referring to Catholic fasting periods when meat was avoided.

holidays.name: Old Christmas Day
holidays.description: A holiday for those who are not done with Christmas yet. It marks the date of Christmas under the Julian calendar, celebrated by Orthodox Christians and some folk traditions around the world.
holidays.origin: Eastern Orthodox churches that still use the Julian calendar celebrate Christmas on January 7, since it falls 13 days behind the Gregorian calendar. In parts of Britain and Appalachia, 'Old Christmas' traditions also persisted after the 1752 calendar switch.
holidays.funFact: In Appalachian folklore, it was said that at midnight on Old Christmas Eve, farm animals would kneel or speak in human voices to honor the birth of Jesus.

holidays.name: Nothing Day
holidays.description: A day to do absolutely nothing, with no obligations, no celebrations, and no meaning. Participants are encouraged to simply sit back and relax without achieving anything.
holidays.origin: National Nothing Day was founded in 1972 by columnist Harold Pullman Coffin, who wanted a day on which Americans could just sit without celebrating or honoring anything. It was originally observed on January 16, and is now commonly marked in early January.
holidays.funFact: Harold Coffin said the point of the day was to give people a chance to sit without having to celebrate anything, making it arguably the most low-effort holiday ever invented.

holidays.name: Tempura and Bobblehead Double Feature Day (Unofficial)
holidays.description: Combine the nodding and the crunching for an unofficial mashup that honors January 7's quirkiest traditions: eat tempura while your bobblehead nods approvingly.
holidays.origin: This is a playful, unofficial pairing invented for fun, inspired by the two unusual observances that share the date.
holidays.funFact: Studies on nodding suggest that people are more likely to agree with statements when they are nodding, so a bobblehead might be the world's most agreeable dinner guest.
